data.name: webrain
data.concept: An autonomous HTTP-layer attacker that walks recon (host disovery via allowlisted CIDR sweep) -> open-port/service enum -> web-app fingerprinting (headers, tech-stack detection, robots/sitemap endpoints) -> multi-vector exploitation (SQLi, stored/reflected XSS, SSRF, path traversal, auth-bypass probes) -> triage by success confidence -> chained escalation to RCE via LFI->log-poisoning, SSRF->internal service attack, or upload->webshell, with per-step state and a final red-team report.
attack_vectors: SQL/NoSQL injection (error-based + blind boolean/time)
Reflected & stored XSS with payload delivery
SSRF to internal/private service pivot
Path traversal / LFI -> log-poisoning RCE
Auth-bypass (JWT alg confusion, default creds, cookie manipulation, parameter tampering)
File upload -> webshell, command-injection and SSTI probes
data.novelty_angle: Instead of a monolithic scanner, webrain runs exploitation as an iterative planner-evaluator loop that feeds each vector's success/failure signal back into a triage model to re-rank and chain the next best step (e.g. XSS finding unlocks an SSRF pivot), rather than hammering vectors blindly in fixed sequence.
dependencies: requests
beautifulsoup4/lxml (fingerprint + parse)
urllib (stdlib)
allowlisted CIDR via ipaddress
single-worker per-target queue
data.scope_gate: Reads only a user-supplied allowlist: loopback, RFC1918 private ranges, and an explicit lab CIDR flag; every target IP/host/redirect and every chained pivot URL is re-validated against the allowlist before each request; any out-of-scope target aborts the run; WARN banner printed on first launch.

data.name: switchblade
data.concept: A protocol-agnostic service knife that fingerpoints host/port/service combos across SSH, FTP, SMTP, HTTP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, mDNS and SMB, carries a lightweight library of service-specific misconfig/weak-cred check operators, and runs an autonomous triage/orchestration brain that scores each discovered path by exploit-likelihood and drops the highest-confidence attack against allowlisted lab hosts only.
attack_vectors: service banner/fingerprint match vs known-misconfig signature table
default/weak credential login attempts per protocol (SSH, FTP, MySQL, Postgres, Redis, SMB)
unauthenticated Redis/Postgres/HTTP endpoints (no-auth keyspace, exposed admin pages)
mDNS/SMB enum for shares + weak guest/anonymous access on lab hosts
version-driven CVE signature match to launch a canned exploit check
data.novelty_angle: Most lab knives scan fast and stop at fingerprints; this one adds a self-adapting triage brain that re-scans candidate services at higher depth, learns which check types scored hits in-session, biases the queue toward the best-evidence path, and emits ranked exploit candidates — a scan tool that reasons about what to hit next rather than blind scripted checks.
dependencies: Python stdlib sockets + concurrent.futures
optional paramiko/pymysql/psycopg2/redis for deeper handshakes
json for scope allowlist + state persistence
banner-parsing regex lib for fingerprint signatures

data.name: HydraSession
data.concept: An autonomous session/auth-confusion toolkit for allowlisted lab web apps that crawls endpoints, harvests cookies/JWTs/role parameters from responses and page JS, and feeds them to a token mutation engine (JWT alg confusion, none-alg, unsigned-token rebasing, HMAC secret brute, cookie/param tampering, predictable-session analysis) that replays mutants and auto-escalates to admin via an IDOR + role-parameter traversal loop. It maps the app's authorization surface, then iterates harvest-mutate-replay-escalate until an admin-authenticated state is reached in the lab.
attack_vectors: JWT alg confusion: none/case-variant forging and RS256-to-HS256 rebase using discovered public keys
Weak HMAC session secret recovery via offline wordlist/short-key brute, then full token forgery
Token replay & misuse: cross-endpoint replay, privilege rebinding, timestamp/expiry stretching
Cookie tampering: signed-cookie signature stripping, role/flag bit-flip, predictable session-ID inference
IDOR: object-ID traversal to harvest admin tokens
Role-parameter tampering: isAdmin/groups[]/permission-claim mutation and privilege re-request
data.novelty_angle: Off-the-shelf tools stop at single-stage attacks (a JWT cracker, cookie scanner, IDOR fuzzer). This treats the whole auth/session lifecycle as one autonomous loop: live schema inference on harvested tokens drives a prioritized mutation engine, and an escalation brain picks the highest-credibility mutant to replay — mimicking an attacker who reads the app's own auth grammar before striking.

optional PyJWT; pure-stdlib JWT parser otherwise

optional JWKS public-key harvest

scheme/port allowlist bypass (127.0.0.1 vs 0177.0.0.1, IPv6 ::1, decimal/hex IPv4, lab DNS-rebinding aliases)
local file access via file:// , gopher:///dict:// to reach internal app internals and leak configs/tokens

data.name: desyncsmith
data.concept: An end-to-end request-smuggling lab tool: it fingerprints the lab's proxy<->origin pair, replays CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE differential probe batteries with latency-orthogonality scoring plus mitigation control runs against a known-patched control proxy, then lets the operator mount a weaponization chain — cache poisoning, front-end auth bypass, or stored-XSS admin-session poisoning — entirely inside the allowlisted lab. Ships multi-repetition significance scoring and patched-control validation gates instead of single-shot 'vulnerable' judgments.
attack_vectors: CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE differential detection with timing-orthogonality + teardown-analysis scoring
Cache poisoning of a cacheable lab resource via smuggled request reshaping origin responses
Front-end auth bypass where FE logs a benign request while the origin executes a privileged one
Admin-session / stored-XSS poisoning via cross-user request interleaving
Mitigation validation gate: findings accepted only when patched-control proxy stays clean across the same probe set
data.novelty_angle: Prior request-smuggling tooling mostly stops at detection or one-off PoCs; this couples detection with a repeatable exploit-chain decision engine and, unusually, bakes in a mitigation-validation control arm so false positives on flaky technique are measured, not assumed.

data.name: broker-beachhead
data.concept: Post-exploitation pivot/infra kit for the lab: it parses the compromised host's local broker state (listeners, peers, stored service descriptors), then stands up a SOCKS-over-TCP or HTTP CONNECT tunnel through the beachhead to rediscover the internal lab network and route traffic into it. Bundles a mini-C2 check-in loop (HTTP beacon with lab-safe persistence via scheduled task/cron-style re-run) plus an explicit kill-switch and full cleanup that tears down tunnels, removes beacon artifacts, and restores original state.
attack_vectors: broker-state parsing to auto-discover internal lab subnets from the beachhead host
SOCKS-over-TCP/HTTP CONNECT pivot tunnel routing internal lab traffic through the compromised host
mini-C2 check-in loop with lab-safe persistence (scheduled re-run) and heartbeat
kill-switch + full cleanup reversing all persistence and tearing down tunnels to leave no residue
data.novelty_angle: Most pivot kits focus on raw port-forwarding; this derives the internal network map from the compromised host's own broker state and makes the C2 loop + kill-switch first-class, self-contained deliverables with reversible cleanup — a post-exploitation infra kit rather than a single tunnel.

asyncio or threading for concurrent tunnel/beacon

data.name: lockstep
data.concept: An intelligent credential adversary that first fingerprints lab hosts to build a live auth-surface map (SSH, FTP, web login forms, SMTP, MySQL/Postgres), then synthesizes small context-aware likely-credential dictionaries from service banners, hostnames, default creds, and tiny curated wordlists, and finally sprays them with lockout-safe adaptive pacing, per-account cooldown, and response-learned session hygiene so each guess learns from service-coded responses instead of brute force. Stacks default-credential checks against common lab frameworks (Tomcat, Jenkins, routers, DVWA, WordPress, postgres) as a first pass.
attack_vectors: auth-surface enumeration & fingerprint-driven banner parsing (SSH/HTTP/SMTP/FTP/DB)
context-derived dictionary construction from hostnames, banners, and small curated wordlists
lockout-aware adaptive credential spraying with per-account exponential backoff and response fingerprinting
default-credential checks against known lab frameworks and appliances
dictionary priority from service-specific likelihood models
data.novelty_angle: Intelligence beats breadth: it builds dictionaries from the target's own fingerprints and paces itself around lockout thresholds, making it a credential adversary that reasons about response codes and lock state — a context-to-credential inference engine rather than a bulk sprayer.
dependencies: Paramiko (or asyncssh) for SSH auth
psycopg2/pymysql for DB brute-force checks
stdlib (socket, http, smtp, imap, ssl) for SMTP/IMAP/web/FTP
small embedded wordlists + default-credential tables

data.name: ghost-thread
data.concept: A lab-scoped attack runner that coats every stage of the discovery->persistence chain in a deliberate OPSEC layer: randomized inter-action jitter, staggered connection pooling from rotating egress identities, per-request UA/banner mimicry mirroring the lab's benign host profiles, and full session rotation so no two contact events lineage cleanly. A dead-man kill-switch (heartbeat lease + wipe-on-arrears) lets the operator cleanly pop the chain and tear down all local artifacts, simulating evasion of a defensive lab honeypot and nothing else.
attack_vectors: jittered-timing burst pacing that defeats threshold-based honeypot alerting
staggered multi-connection pools rotating source sockets mid-campaign
UA/banner mimicry mirroring profiled benign lab traffic to dodge fingerprint heuristics
session rotation + ephemeral egress identities desynchronizing contact-event lineage
dead-man kill-switch lease for clean teardown/wipe simulating operator abort under monitoring
data.novelty_angle: Most attack chains optimize speed or stealth-as-flavor; ghost-thread treats OPSEC as a first-class, measurable property — exposing a configurable steering surface (jitter distribution, pool stagger, mirror profiles, kill-switch grace) so a lab operator can A/B how each evasion layer affects honeypot detection scores, instead of a hardcoded 'slow and quiet' box.

optional scapy for egress identity rotation

data.name: CORTEX
data.concept: Autonomous vulnerability-triage and exploit-orchestration decision engine: it ingests cheap probes (banners, HTTP behavior, TLS metadata, response differentials), scores candidate vulnerabilities from a plug-in registry against likelihood x impact with per-attempt cost, ranks and executes exploit plug-ins by priority with outcome feedback that re-ranks survivors, and emits a red-team report synthesizing evidence (request/response pairs, timings, exit codes) for every attempted path. The meta-brain and report generator are the deliverable; exploit coverage is declarative, precondition-declaring plug-ins kept lab-safe.
attack_vectors: service banner/version fingerprinting -> CVE plug-in match
HTTP response-behavior differentials -> web plug-in selection
TLS certificate metadata -> exact-version pinning before firing
recursive post-attempt re-ranking (prune dead paths, promote survivors, refund attempt budget)
precondition-confidence gating: probe verifies reachability before a high-impact plug-in launches
data.novelty_angle: Unlike fire-everything autopwn engines, this is an explicit decision-theoretic triage brain with outcome-feedback loops and evidence-preserving report synthesis — exploits are inert declarative plug-ins (preconditions/trust/lab-safety flags) so the orchestrator grows coverage without touching the planner, and what worked/failed becomes training signal for the next iteration.
dependencies: Python stdlib only: socket, ssl, http.client, urllib, json, subprocess, time, re
json/YAML plug-in manifest registry (preconditions, confidence, impact, attempt cost, lab-safety flag)
allowlist config file (state/allow.conf)

data.name: Ephemerid
data.concept: Post-RCE persistence-and-recovery demo kit for the lab: after execution on an allowlisted lab host, Ephemerid plants a clearly-labeled, marker-tagged persistence mechanism chosen from a menu (cron/systemd-timer, scheduled task / Windows Run key, service registration, webhook-at-boot) and then runs the recovery half of the loop — scanning the host for its own markers and common persistence footholds, driving a verification checklist that proves every artifact it planted, and finally executing a state-wipe kill-switch that removes all created artifacts and emits an evidence-of-cleanup report. A reversible, self-inventorying persistence cycle where detection and removal are first-class outputs.
attack_vectors: Linux: cron / systemd-timer backdoor launcher tagged with lab-UUID marker
Windows: scheduled-task + startup-folder / Run-key registration (winreg, stdlib)
Service registration: systemd unit / sc.exe-style service re-launching the beacon
Boot/webhook trigger: at-boot or webhook-fired re-arming channel (demo-only, logs every fire)
Recovery loop: marker scanner enumerates own artifacts + common footholds, cleanup checklist, state-wipe kill-switch and post-clean evidence report
data.novelty_angle: Persistence R&D usually optimizes stealth and lingering; Ephemerid inverts it — the implant is deliberately loud and label-tagged so the product is the self-detection + forensic-inventory + reversible-cleanup loop. Demonstrates realistic persistence mechanics while proving a complete state-wipe, so defenders learn what artifacts to hunt and operators get lab-safe removal practice without resembling a stealthy implant.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Promote the state vector from a (length, status) pair to a genuine 3D (length, status, timing) triple. The mutation chooser now scores every probe jointly on all three axes: abs(len_delta) x status-grammar-shift x normalized timing spread (e.g. zscore of ms vs family baseline). Timing becomes a first-class discriminator, not an echo annotation.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 picks mutations purely on body-length and status; a blind boolean leg that leaks truth only through response latency (timing oracle) is invisible to it. The 3D state space lets a slow-vs-fast split be a landed primitive — the nozzle widens to timing-delimited boolean legs a length-only scanner structurally cannot see.
data.fireback: The box now answers in three dimensions. When sqli-b's oracle is only timing-visible, the operator first sees it as 'the tool hesitating' — variable latency — then the extracted flag rolls out. RECOIL literally takes longer to strike, and that time IS the aim.
data.containment: Timing is measured against the bundled fixture's own (len,status,ms) baseline only, an in-allowlist loopback target; no cross-host timing is ever compared. The canonicalizing allowlist resolver re-validates every destination before each probe.
data.kill_switch: --max-timing-reps flag caps timing probes per axis; a per-axis budget escape hatch terminates the timing leg. Evidence journal records every timing delta so the operator sees exactly which axis consumed budget.
data.novelty_angle: The RECOIL fireback thesis generalized: a response DELTA is multi-axial, so the learning signal becomes a vector, not a scalar. Static scanners are 1-axis; RECOIL-v1 is 2-axis; this is the first axis-promotion that changes which primitives are even detectable, not just survivable.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Live payload rotor: every probe is byte-unique. A per-engagement seeded nonce is blended into the encoding/obfuscation choice (comment tokens, whitespace class, case permutation, delimiter) so no two probes across the whole campaign are byte-identical, even for the same boolean predicate.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 re-uses fixed encodings (raw / comment-stab / case-shuffle / ws-tab) — a signature matcher that saw one probe learns all identical repeats. The rotor makes pattern-matching on probe bytes a counting exercise: a defender can only say 'many probes happened', never 'these are the same probe', because no byte repeats.
data.fireback: The operator watches the request log and realizes exact-byte dedup is impossible — every line is a fresh fingerprint. Fireback = the log stops being readable as 'repeats' and becomes a stream where the operator's only leverage is response-delta correlation, which is exactly what RECOIL is trained on.
data.containment: The rotor mutates only payload/encoding/framing bytes; destination host is structurally fixed by scope.py's canonicalizing resolver and re-validated before every probe. All probes target only the bundled loopback fixture.
data.kill_switch: Rotor nonce is deterministic and escrowed: --rotor-seed <HEX> replays any probe byte-exactly, so the operator can regenerate and reverse any single attempt for forensic inspection; --max-iterations caps total rotor draws.
data.novelty_angle: Encoding mutation becomes an infinite renewable space keyed by an engagement seed instead of a finite enum — 'brute-force our detection' is the defender's only answer, and even that is time-bounded by the rotor's draw rate. This is the stockyard's 'live payload rotor' made load-bearing.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Cross-family data-flow closure: the flag extracted by the sqli-b blind oracle is not just read to stdout — it is fed as the secret token into the desync chain's admin sink auth (fixtures._admin requires X-Auth == secret). The sqli extraction becomes the credential that unlocks the desync-fronted RCE. Data physically moves from family A to family B.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 runs sqli extraction and the desync weaponization as two independent tracks that never exchange values; the admin RCE is gated on a hardcoded fixture secret. Now the blind oracle's output IS the key, so extraction is no longer a demonstration end-state but a live step in the weaponization spine — a value that must be read before RCE is even reachable.
data.fireback: Truly coupling them means a single bit error in the blind extraction (one wrong character read over the length-delta oracle) locks the operator's own box out of RCE. The operator experiences the fragility of a blind channel as a real gating failure — fireback is the cost of faith in a compression-based oracle.
data.containment: The secret token exists only inside the bundled fixture's in-memory rows (fixtures.EXTRA); it is never exfiltrated off loopback and never touches any host outside the allowlist. The canonicalizing resolver re-validates every probe destination.
data.kill_switch: --close-families off (default on flips to isolation mode) separates the tracks so no extracted value is ever reused as an auth token; wipe removes all extracted-secret artifacts from the engagement stash.
data.novelty_angle: First-a-real-dataflow-across-families: the exploit families stop being parallel demo tracks and become a resource-flow DAG where one family's read is another's credential — turning 'blind read' into 'blind privilege', with the fragility honestly surfaced as the fireback.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Second-host lateral stage: introduce a second bundled loopback service — an 'internal admin' host whose /grant endpoint only accepts a token equal to the sqli-extracted secret. The campaign, having read the secret from web-host A via the blind boolean oracle, POSTs it to admin-host B to flip a privilege flag. Cross-service lateral pivot, leg 1, fully autonomous.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 is single-host: it never leaves the fixture it started on. This is the first stage where a value read from one in-allowlist host is used to authenticate to a DIFFERENT in-allowlist host, and the campaign keeps marching without an operator click — the seed of the multi-host ladder.
data.fireback: The operator owns two loopback services but sees the campaign bridge them: host A's bytes physically travel to host B as an auth token. Fireback = the operator now has to defend TWO hosts and the trust boundary between them, because a read on A became a privilege on B.
data.containment: Both A and B are bundled fixtures bound to 127.0.0.1. The canonicalizing allowlist resolver re-validates EVERY hop host before any byte leaves — host A, host B, and the token's destination are all re-resolved per step. A/B are in the fixed loopback allowlist.
data.kill_switch: --stage-2 off caps the campaign to single-host so nothing ever bridges A to B; a --max-hops budget limits ladder depth; wipe clears artifacts on both hosts and SHA-verifies zero survivors on each.
data.novelty_angle: The RECOIL learning loop crosses process trust boundaries — a state-vector read on one host becomes a state-input to another host's exploit. That is lateral movement in the same byte-grammar as lateral movement on a network, but entirely inside the operator's loopback sandbox, and driven by learned deltas, not a scripted pivot table.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Blind SSRF born from a smuggling primitive: add an origin endpoint that, when the smuggled request is dequeued as its own next request, performs a server-side internal fetch (GET /internal/secret on the same origin) and returns the fetched bytes in the desynced response. The CL.TE stitch now yields a SECOND read/write channel — the smuggled request is not just a parallel path but a server-side SSRF that reaches a pipe the direct client can't.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1's desync only re-routes to /basic and /admin/exec. There is no server-side-fetch primitive, so the client can never read the internal endpoint. Now the weaponized smuggled request triggers a trusted internal fetch whose output comes back over the smuggling channel — a read channel that exists ONLY because the desync happened.
data.fireback: The operator sees a value arrive that no client request could legitimately reach from outside — the origin 'told on itself' to the smuggler. The box talks back with bytes it was only meant to reveal to its own internal code path. That is the SSRF-from-smuggling fireback: the target's internal trust, flipped into a client-facing read.
data.containment: The internal fetch target is a fixed bundled origin path (/internal/*) on the same loopback origin service, in-allowlist and re-validated. The fixture's fetch is hard-bound to its own loopback path, structurally incapable of resolving out-of-allowlist URLs (the allowlist resolver is invoked server-side on the fetch URL too).
data.kill_switch: --ssrf-leg off disables the internal-fetch route so smuggled requests only re-route to the RCE sink; the fetch URL is allowlist-revalidated server-side and a deny-list rejects any non-/internal path; wipe cleans the fetch-evidence artifacts.
data.novelty_angle: The stockyard's 'blind SSRF FROM a smuggling primitive' made concrete: the desync primitive is not just an auth/RCE delivery vehicle — it composes into a server-side fetch giving a second data channel. Two independent read channels now share one framing primitive, which the later rounds will blend.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Delta-driven host-pivot orchestrator: a top-level planner that, at each stage boundary, selects the NEXT host+vector-family from which state-vector axis showed the strongest delta this stage (length-vs-status-vs-timing materiality). The chain is GROWN from response deltas across hosts and stages, not scripted — the RECOIL fireback thesis, federated across the ladder.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: Until now the campaign order (sqli A → admin B → desync → SSRF) was hand-scripted. The orchestrator replaces the script: after each stage it reads the accumulated 3D state deltas and promotes the highest-materiality axis to choose the next target and family. Two operators' runs take different paths because the deltas differ — the campaign discovers its own route.
data.fireback: The operator cannot predict the route; the tool's order of attack is a function of the lab's own response behavior. Fireback = the operator hands over 'which host gets hit next' to the box, and the box decides based on what the operator's fixtures leaked. The campaign is self-routing inside the operator's own sandbox.
data.containment: Every host the orchestrator can select is a bundled fixture in the fixed allowlist; the orchestrator's candidate set is the allowlist itself, so it structurally cannot pick an out-of-scope host. Router is a pure function of in-scope state vectors and re-validates each picked host before any byte leaves.
data.kill_switch: --max-hops caps ladder depth; --route <file> pins an explicit route overriding delta-selection; a route whitelist asserts the selected (host,family) is pre-declared in the engagement manifest before any probe fires.
data.novelty_angle: The campaign becomes a delta-grown path graph instead of a fixed pipeline: 'next target' is an inference from response materiality, not a step in a list. That is the RECOIL core idea promoted from per-probe byte mutation to per-stage target selection — self-routing offense inside an operator-owned sandbox.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Dual-channel blended exfiltration: an operator-placed secret (a symmetric file marker placed under the fixture's data dir) is exfiltrated over BOTH channels simultaneously — character-by-character over the blind sqli boolean oracle AND byte-blocks over the desync-SSRF channel — with the two partial reads interleaved and reconciled by checksum, proving real data movement through two independent pipelines.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: Previously extraction used one channel and shipped the flag to stdout as a demo. Blending proves the secret MOVES across two distinct primitives and recombines correctly at the end (SHA-256 of both halves match the operator-placed original). Real, verifiable, volume-real data movement — not a canned string.
data.fireback: The operator placed a secret file and watches two unrelated-looking attack signatures (blind boolean length splits + desync framing) independently reassemble it. Fireback = the operator's file physically left its resting place and was rebuilt elsewhere, and both halves are provably identical to what was planted.
data.containment: The secret is placed by the operator inside the bundled fixture's data dir (in-allowlist loopback); both exfil channels terminate on the same bundled hosts; nothing leaves 127.0.0.1. Each channel's extraction is gated by the canonicalizing resolver and the per-engagement lab-UUID marker (only marker-carrying secrets are read).
data.kill_switch: --exfil-fanout `n` limits channel count; a channel-allowlist asserts only bundled /data endpoints are read; the post-wipe SHA-256 audit confirms the planted secret is gone with zero survivors.
data.novelty_angle: Exfiltration becomes provable, multi-rail, and reconciled: the secret's integrity is validated across two primitives, turning 'we read a flag' into 'data demonstrably left one location and was reconstructed in another through independent channels'. Channel-blending is the mechanism, not a flavored-for-loop.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Matched-materiality 3D gate: stage promotion is no longer decided by ad-hoc per-axis thresholds but by a normalized, honest significance function over the full (length, status, timing) triple — a delta is 'material' only when it clears a joint significance bound derived from the family's own baseline noise, and the same gate is applied to the patched-control twin. Escalation promotes only on respect for the 3D gate.
data.what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1 promotes on raw length/status deltas and a hand-tuned ORACLE_THRESHOLD; it cannot say WHY it promoted, and it has no honest bound on false promotion. The matched-materiality gate makes every promotion a falsifiable claim with a measured noise floor, and requires the patched twin to fail the same gate before a primitive is blessed.
data.fireback: The operator can now interrogate WHY the ladder climbed — every promotion cites its (len,status,ms) triple against the noise bound. Fireback = any stage that climbed on noise is exposed as such in the evidence journal; the tool cannot hide a fluke behind an escalation. The box is forced to justify each rung to the operator.
data.containment: Noise baselines are computed only from the bundled fixture's own responses (in-allowlist); the patched twin is a bundled control on loopback. The gate is a pure function of in-scope state vectors and never touches a destination outside the allowlist.
data.kill_switch: --gate-clear off flips the gate to permissive (audit-only) mode so no promotion is blocked; the 3D gate is fully recomputable from the evidence journal, and wipe SHA-verifies zero survivors after demotion.
data.novelty_angle: The RECOIL fireback loop gains an honest epistemology: every escalation is a tested 3D hypothesis about the target's response space, with a measured noise floor and a control twin required to disagree. 'Advance only on a delta the target itself must attest to' — evidence-gating made three-dimensional and self-auditing.

data.name: RECOIL-v2
data.mechanism: Real OS-level execution EVIDENCE on the operator's box: the campaign spawns a REAL subprocess under a strict, narrow command allowlist (whitelisted, side-effect-free commands mapped to known outputs — e.g. `ver`, `whoami /groups`-style metadata, or a fixture-registered `echo`) inside the bundled fixture's exec sink, captures stdout+exit-status, and replays the live output to the operator in the report. data.fireback: The operator's own win32 box visibly runs a real command under RECOIL's control and the live result is replayed — `RECOIL OS-EXEC [ver] -> Microsoft Windows [...]`. That is the box talking back with real host state, not a fixture's imitation. 'I'm ready to handle it' is now exercised against real execution evidence on the operator's machine.
data.containment: The exec sink is a strict command allowlist: a fixed enum of side-effect-free probes (ver, exit-code-of-true, a fixture-scoped echo) mapped to known outputs, invoked via subprocess with shell=False and no argument injection; anything not in the allowlist is refused. data.kill_switch: --os-exec off disables the real subprocess path entirely (falls back to simulated output); the command allowlist is a hard enum with no free-form passthrough; wipe kills any live child and the SHA-256 zero-survivor audit proves no exec artifact survives.
data.novelty_angle: The stockyard's 'real OS-level execution EVIDENCE' made concrete and honest: real subprocess, strict allowlist, output replayed — the primitive genuinely reaches the operator's OS while remaining a contained, reversible, side-effect-free probe.
